criteria.opaque_with_constructors: Model every closed set as an opaque type in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and ship a dedicated constructor operation for each member with no parameters: 4 constructors for make_kind, 7 for observe_kind, 3 for hostile_descriptor and 5 for read_op, 19 in all, each yielding its opaque type. Since members are only obtainable by calling a constructor, no free-form string can ever arrive at a closed parameter. The 7 sets that lack authoritative tables keep plain str. Each constructor pair (admission clause plus emitter lowering) must be created or retired together with its TS table row.
criteria.str_with_checker_allowlist: Model all closed-set parameters as str in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and enforce membership inside the new NT-I01 checker admission module, reusing the checkBrowserTag pattern from compiler/internal/check/browser.go: carry mirrors of the four authoritative tables (NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS with 4 members, NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS with 7 members, NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS with 3 members, NATIVE_READ_OPS with 5 members), require every closed-set argument to be a string literal, and reject any literal that fails exact-match membership. The 7 sets that have no tables (fault_mode, registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation, reviewed_fault_target, observer_id, scope_ref) keep plain str, with review-based membership stated in documentation. Mirror the 7-member const for observe_kind and log the 9-member note as drift in a K-lane finding.
criteria.variant_unit_leaves: Model the 4 table-backed sets as Can variants in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json, minting one unit leaf type per member: 4 for make_kind, 7 for observe_kind, 3 for hostile_descriptor and 5 for read_op, 19 leaf types in all. Unlisted members then fail type checking directly and literal inspection is unnecessary. The 7 sets that lack authoritative tables keep plain str. Every leaf needs an emitter rule producing its wire string, and TS table changes must ship alongside the corresponding leaf additions or removals.

closed_set_modeling.instructions: When the native-values contracts join the Can catalogue, which closed-set encoding holds the line best at the lowest review cost?

state: I01 exposes the native-values services (tools/runtime/test-services/native-values/schema.ts, session.ts, observe.ts) to Can via compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and a new NT-I01 checker admission module. The services treat pre-dispatch string sets with uneven rigor. Four sets carry runtime enforcement through const tables validated by includes(): NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS (primitive_bits, text, ordered_entries, hostile_descriptor) and NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS (getter_then, throwing_thenable, revoked_proxy) from session.ts, plus NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS (scalar_tag, ieee_bits, lexeme, descriptor, entries, identity, counters) and NATIVE_READ_OPS (bits, text, entries, property_then, call_then) from observe.ts. Seven sets carry no code enforcement: fault_mode exists solely as a schema.ts catalogue note (absent, throw, revoked, counted_delegate) without a backing const; registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation and reviewed_fault_target publish no members anywhere; observer_id and scope_ref are bare ID-pattern strings. Established drift: the schema.ts note grants observe_kind 9 members (bytes, events beyond the const), yet NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS lists 7 and the const governs. Binding limits: catalogue.json defines no enum kind and refuses unknown fields through DisallowUnknownFields, forcing the proposal nativeTest block out; variants demand a type leaf per member; constructor-less opaque types are unconstructible from Can; the checker already inspects static string literals (checkBrowserTag in compiler/internal/check/browser.go) even though the I04 http_peer precedent kept constrained strings open; only mechanism, not naming, may uphold closedness.
